body:
**Starts** once #251 is merged.

**Joe's setup is done** for the harness this issue uses, Claude Code with Sonnet (2026-11-04). The bot user is `claude-code-sonnet@jjk3.com`, user ID `d37cc40c-3a8f-4ece-ba59-f1309c7b3e39`, from `whoami`. Its account file is `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/claude-code-sonnet.env`. Claude Code's own config folder, `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude/`, is signed in, and its command timeout is raised and checked. So the work needs nothing more from Joe, unless a fix changes the design.

## Why

Agent evaluations (#53) need recorded sessions to score, and planning a whole trip by hand takes a long conversation. A **simulated user** is a coding agent harness, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode, with a chosen model, that plays a user planning a trip. It chats with the app through `npm run live-chat` (#251), the terminal client that does what the browser does. Different harnesses and models play a user a little differently, which gives the evaluations more varied sessions than Joe and his family can make by hand.

This issue sets up how a simulated user works, and shakes it out with one whole trip on the local stack, where traces are throwaway. #67 and #68 then record the first trips on the live site, for the corpus.

**The two Phoenix projects have different jobs here.** `road-trip-agent-local` is for development and tests, and its traces are throwaway. `road-trip-agent`, the server's project, holds the sessions to be evaluated, annotated, and scored (systems design, section 10). So shakedown runs point `live-chat` at the local stack, and recorded trips point it at the live site.

## Design

- [Agent evaluations](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/issues/53), the bullet "How are the evaluations built up?" in its open questions: what a scenario file holds, and how the simulated user should act.
- [Systems design](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/systems.md), section 3 (sign-in) and section 10 (traces).
- [Domain model](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/domain-model.md), section 5.1: the San Francisco trip.

Terms used here:

- **Harness:** the coding agent program that runs the model, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode.
- **Bot user:** a Supabase user made for one harness and model pair, such as one for Codex with a GPT model. Its email is named harness-model, so it's clear which one it is. Each turn's span in Phoenix has the user's ID (`user.id`), so the bot user tells which harness and model played a session.
- **Trip file:** what the user knows and does on one trip: the facts, what's not decided yet, the changes partway through, and when the trip counts as planned.
- **Persona file:** how the user talks, on any trip, such as curt or impatient. A run pairs one trip file with one persona file, so any persona can play any trip.
- **Run folder:** a folder outside the repo, made for one run of one bot user on one trip with one persona. The harness starts there, and the folder holds only what that run needs.

## Open questions

- ~~Does the simulated user run in the repo, or in a folder outside it? In the repo, it can read the coordinator's prompts, the design docs, and the example trips, so it could know more than a real user would. It could also run other commands, such as against the local database. Outside the repo, it would get only its scenario file and its instructions, plus a short script that runs `npm run live-chat` from the repo. Joe isn't sure it's needed. Raised on 2026-11-04, in chat.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat: outside the repo, in a run folder of its own. Harnesses poke around their working folder, so a folder holding every trip and persona would let a simulated user read the ones it isn't playing. And a folder inside the repo loads the repo's `CLAUDE.md` on its own, since Claude Code reads every `CLAUDE.md` from its folder up. The setup is in Do.
- ~~How does a scenario run that needs a later date, such as "on May 8, 2027, the user opens the trip again"? The live site always uses today's date, and nothing sets it. Until this is settled, scenarios leave such steps out. Raised on 2026-11-04, in chat.~~ Settled by Joe on 2026-11-04, in chat: the San Francisco and Moab trip files leave out steps tied to a date, and nothing fakes the date. Faking it would take fake weather too, since Google gives forecasts only for the real next 10 days or so. And Claude Code's own date line, from the real clock, would show the coordinator two different dates, which technical spec 5.2 rules out. The forecast offer, which those steps were for, gets a trip of its own that starts for real a few days after the run (#259).

## Do

- Make a `simulated-users/` folder in the repo. It holds:
  - `instructions.md`, what every simulated user gets.
  - `trips/`, one trip file per trip.
  - `personas/`, one persona file per persona.
  - `bot-users.md`, each bot user's ID with its email.
  - `README.md`, how to add a bot user, set up a run, and start each harness. Joe refers to it, so it has to work on its own.
- A trip file holds:
  - the facts the user knows, such as dates, places, budget, and driving limits.
  - things the user hasn't decided yet.
  - changes to make partway through, and when, such as skipping Denver once the first draft is done.
  - when the trip counts as planned, so the simulated user knows when to stop.

  The facts also work as an answer key, to check what the coordinator saved to the trip brief. A persona file holds only how the user talks and acts, with nothing about any one trip.
- Add a setup script that makes a run folder, such as `npm run sim-setup -- codex-gpt-5 moab curt`, for a bot user, a trip, and a persona. It also takes the site, local or live. The folder goes in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/`, named for the three, such as `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/codex-gpt-5-moab-curt/`. It stops if that folder is already there, so an old run's files never mix with a new one. The folder gets:
  - `instructions.md`, and copies of the trip file and the persona file named plainly `trip.md` and `persona.md`, so nothing in the folder hints at other trips.
  - `account.env`, the bot user's email and password from `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, plus `LIVE_CHAT_SITE` for the site. It uses the names `live-chat` already reads: `LIVE_CHAT_SITE`, `LIVE_CHAT_EMAIL`, and `LIVE_CHAT_PASSWORD`.
  - `chat.sh`, which loads `account.env` and runs `npm run live-chat` in the repo, passing its arguments and standard input through. Values set in the shell win over the repo's `.env`, so the bot user's values are the ones used.
- The instructions say how to use `./chat.sh`: starting the trip, sending messages, looking at the option cards and the itinerary, and using the card buttons. They also say how to act: answer only what's asked, give one or two facts at a time, and stick with any answer it makes up. A web user sees the cards and the itinerary beside the chat without asking, so the instructions say to look at them as a user would, such as after a reply says a card is open.
- Write down how to add a harness:
  - Joe makes one bot user per harness and model pair, in the Supabase dashboard (systems design, section 3). Its email and password go in `~/tmp/road-trip-sims/accounts/<bot user>.env`, outside the repo, so they can't be committed.
  - Keep a list in the repo of each bot user's ID with its email, starting with the bot user above, so a session in Phoenix can be traced to who played it. Phoenix shows only the user's ID. Each line comes from running `npm run live-chat`'s `whoami` as that bot user. No passwords in the list.
  - Each harness starts in the run folder, so it doesn't load the repo's `CLAUDE.md`. Joe's own `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` still loads for some harnesses, so the README gives each one's start command:
    - Claude Code: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude --model <model>`. Its own config folder keeps out Joe's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, and memory. Joe signs in once in that config folder.
    - Codex: `codex -m <model>`. It reads only `AGENTS.md`, and Joe has none.
    - opencode: `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE=1 opencode -m <model>`. opencode falls back to `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` when it has no `AGENTS.md` of its own.

    Every harness then gets the same opening prompt, such as "Read instructions.md, trip.md, and persona.md, then plan the trip."
  - Check the harness lets a shell command it waits on run at least 5 minutes, since a turn with workers can take about 4. Ask it to run `python3 -c 'import time; time.sleep(330)'; echo done` in the foreground, without setting a timeout itself. If it doesn't print "done", raise the harness's command timeout in its settings, and try again. Don't use `sleep` for the check: Claude Code refuses a foreground `sleep`, and runs it in the background, where there's no limit to test. Claude Code cuts a command off after 2 minutes by default. Its config folder's `settings.json` raises that with `"env": { "BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000", "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "600000" }`. Checked on 2026-11-04 with Claude Code 2.1.318.
- Write the San Francisco trip file, from domain model section 5.1, with changes partway through, and one persona file. The trip is planned in one session. A change may start a new session right away, but never on a later day, so leave out changes such as the user opening the trip again on May 8, 2027. Joe decided on 2026-11-04, in chat, that coming back to a trip later isn't tested here. The San Francisco changes in the design walkthroughs' last prompt (`reviews/walkthroughs/prompt-6.md`, section "Changes to make along the way") are a starting point. That prompt is out of date, so check each change still fits the current design.
- Run the whole San Francisco trip with Claude Code and Sonnet against the local stack (`npm run dev`), signed in as its bot user. The implementer starts it, headless, in the run folder: `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=~/tmp/road-trip-sims/.claude claude -p --model sonnet --allowedTools "Bash(./chat.sh:*)"`, in the background, and reads the session when it ends. Give the opening prompt on standard input, since `--allowedTools` takes a list and would read a prompt after it as one more tool. Allow more tools only if the run shows the simulated user needs them. Fix the problems it finds in the setup, the trip file, the persona file, or the instructions. File any app bug as a new issue. A fix that changes the design goes to Joe first.
- In DEVELOPMENT.md section 5, point to `simulated-users/README.md` for how to run a simulated user.

## Done when

- One harness plays the San Francisco trip from start to finish against the local stack, and stops when the trip file says the trip is planned.
- Each problem the run found is fixed, or filed as an issue.
- A new harness can be added, and a run set up and started, from `simulated-users/README.md`, with no other help.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

Reworked on 2026-11-04: the simulated user moved from a script that runs Claude as the user to any harness and model, through `npm run live-chat`. The report comparing the final itinerary with domain model section 5 came out, since #67 and #68 no longer check that. Later on 2026-11-04: the scenario file split into a trip file and a persona file, and each run got its own folder outside the repo.

## Why

A **simulated user** is a coding agent harness, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode, with a chosen model, that plays a user planning a trip. It chats with the app through `npm run live-chat` (#251), the terminal client that does what the browser does. Different harnesses and models play a user a little differently, which gives the evaluations more varied sessions than Joe and his family can make by hand.

This issue sets up how a simulated user works, and shakes it out with one whole trip on the local stack, where traces are throwaway. #67 and #68 then record the first trips on the live site, for the corpus.

**The two Phoenix projects have different jobs here.** `road-trip-agent-local` is for development and tests, and its traces are throwaway. `road-trip-agent`, the server's project, holds the sessions to be evaluated, annotated, and scored (systems design, section 10). So shakedown runs point `live-chat` at the local stack, and recorded trips point it at the live site.

Terms used here:

- **Harness:** the coding agent program that runs the model, such as Claude Code, Codex, or opencode.
- **Bot user:** a Supabase user made for one harness and model pair, such as one for Codex with a GPT model. Its email is named harness-model, so it's clear which one it is. Each turn's span in Phoenix has the user's ID (`user.id`), so the bot user tells which harness and model played a session.
- **Trip file:** what the user knows and does on one trip: the facts, what's not decided yet, the changes partway through, and when the trip counts as planned.
- **Persona file:** how the user talks, on any trip, such as curt or impatient. A run pairs one trip file with one persona file, so any persona can play any trip.
- **Run folder:** a folder outside the repo, made for one run of one bot user on one trip with one persona. The harness starts there, and the folder holds only what that run needs.
